response.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) * 1.0 / NULLIF(AVG(HCT), 0) AS ratio FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING AVG(HGB) IS NOT NULL AND AVG(HCT) IS NOT NULL AND AVG(HCT) <> 0), a1 AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg1 FROM r), k1 AS (SELECT r.ID, r.ratio, r.ratio - a1.avg1 AS diff1 FROM r, a1 WHERE r.ratio > a1.avg1), a2 AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg2 FROM k1), k2 AS (SELECT k1.ID, k1.ratio, k1.diff1, k1.ratio - a2.avg2 AS diff2 FROM k1, a2 WHERE k1.ratio > a2.avg2) SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio, AVG(diff1) AS avg_above_overall_avg, AVG(diff2) AS avg_above_second_avg FROM k2

assumptions.assumption: The overall average ratio is the unweighted mean of the per-patient ratios, one value per patient. It is not a pooled ratio computed over all lab rows.
Patients with no non-null HGB or no non-null HCT, or with an average HCT of 0, have no defined ratio. They are excluded from the overall average and from the later steps.
The second average is the mean of the ratios of the patients kept in the first step.
